jurisdiction_sources.note: 16 V.S.A. section 603(a) inventory: Windsor Central Unified Union School District, styled Mountain Views School District, a modified unified union district that is its own supervisory district (Mountain Views SU; member towns: Barnard (grades 7-12 only), Bridgewater, Killington, Plymouth, Pomfret, Reading, Woodstock). Operates PK-12.
Mountain Views School District / Mountain Views SU (official site).

sources.note: Mountain Views SD Annual Meeting Warning 2026 (official), Article 9: "The legal voters of the specified towns designated within this itemized Article shall elect the following: Killington: one school director... Plymouth: one... Pomfret: one... Reading: one school director AND one director to complete the remaining two years of a three-year term; Woodstock: two school directors AND one director to complete the one remaining year of a three-year term" -- town-only electorates (the 2024 warning, Art. 5, is in the same "shall elect only their director(s)" form). Board: 18 seats -- Woodstock 6, each other town 2 (State Board formation minutes describe the pre-Barnard board as 16 on this allocation; Barnard's accession added 2).

Mountain Views SD board minutes, December 2, 2024 (official) -- the newest official minutes located; the roster is assembled from the district's minutes series (March 2023 - December 2024), cross-checked against the SU's October 14, 2025 press release (which labels Ryan Townsend "Bridgewater" and Josh Linton "Plymouth"). The district publishes NO roster page and NO term expirations, and the March 3, 2026 election winners are undocumented in any fetched official source (missing: the district's March 2026 returns / reorganization minutes) -- the minted roster is as of the December 2024 minutes and the October 2025 press release, flagged.

board.post_note: MODEL: one post per member town (proportional, town-only electorates, 16 V.S.A. section 730(a)(1) pattern). Two seats are HELD: Matt Stout holds either Killington's second seat or Woodstock's sixth (the minutes' two-column layout jumbles his placement; only a news item calls him "of Woodstock"), and the other of those seats' holder is unnamed in any fetched official source. Barnard members sit for all district business in the minutes although Barnard participates for grades 7-12 only.
